The ¹H NMR shows 15 total protons: a 10 H multiplet at 1.35 ppm (likely five CH₂ groups), a 1 H multiplet at 2.63 ppm (a methine coupled to the cyclohexyl protons), and an AA′BB′ aromatic pattern (4 H, 7.24 ppm and 7.41 ppm). This pattern fits a para‑disubstituted benzene
To pinpoint the exact substituent, I'll request the ¹³C NMR spectrum, which will reveal how many distinct carbon environments are present and whether a carbonyl or other functional group is present.
No carbonyl or hetero‑atom signals are present, so the second para substituent must be a non‑protonated, non‑hetero atom group such as a halogen.

The simplest structure matching these data is para‑bromo‑(or chloro‑)cyclohexylbenzene, i.e., a benzene ring bearing a cyclohexyl group at one para position and a bromine (or chlorine) at the opposite para position.
Both give the same NMR pattern; the exact halogen can be distinguished by mass spectrometry. I will retrieve the mass spectrum to see the molecular ion and confirm the halogen.

Cl atomic mass 34.968852. Subtract from 194.0862 gives 159.11735 for C+H mass... C12H15Cl gives mass: 144 + 15*1.007825=144+15.117375=159.117375 + 34.968852 = 194.086227. Perfect! So formula C12H15Cl.
The structure that fits all data is a para‑chloro‑substituted phenyl attached directly to a cyclohexyl ring. The corresponding SMILES string is: Clc1ccc(cc1)C2CCCCC2.
